pages.title: Welcome to the Green World of Plants
bulletPoints: Plants cover our Earth like a giant green blanket and give us clean air to breathe.
From tiny soft green grass blades to giant oak trees, plants are living beings.
Plants drink sunshine and make their own food through magic green leaves.
Observation: Spot three different green leaves in your garden or school playground.

pages.title: The Five Main Parts of a Plant
bulletPoints: Roots: Grow underground like anchors, drinking water and healthy minerals from soil.
Stem: The strong green elevator that carries water up to leaves and flowers.
Leaves: The sunny green kitchens where plant food is lovingly cooked.
Flowers & Fruits: Colorful petals that attract butterflies and grow sweet fruit with seeds.

pages.title: Underground Wonders: The Roots
bulletPoints: Taproots: One big thick main root going deep down (like carrots, radishes, and beetroots).
Fibrous Roots: A bunch of bushy, thin hair-like roots spreading out (like grass, wheat, and onion).
How roots protect our soil: Root networks hold dirt tightly so rain cannot wash it away.
Experiment: Put a celery stalk in blue colored water to watch roots pull water upwards!

pages.title: Stems: The Plant's Super Highway
bulletPoints: Green soft stems: Found on herbs like coriander and mint that bend easily in the wind.
Woody strong stems: Found on rose bushes and hibiscus shrubs that stay firm.
Trunk: The massive thick wooden stem of great trees covered in rough protective bark.
Underground stems: Potatoes, ginger, and onions store lots of food safe underground!

pages.title: Leaves: Nature's Solar Kitchens
bulletPoints: Chlorophyll: The special green pigment that catches warm yellow sunlight.
Photosynthesis: The recipe where leaves combine sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
Stomata: Tiny microscopic breathing mouths on the underside of leaves.
The gift of plants: In exchange for carbon dioxide, green leaves release pure fresh oxygen!

pages.title: Colorful Flowers & Busy Bees
bulletPoints: Petals: Bright red, yellow, and purple colors that invite busy honeybees and hummingbirds.
Nectar: The sweet sugary drink flowers offer to visiting pollinators.
Pollen grains: Fine golden dust that bees carry from flower to flower to help them make seeds.
Sweet scents: Jasmine and roses release lovely perfumes into the evening breeze.

pages.title: Fruits: Delicious Seed Protectors
bulletPoints: A flower fades away and gently swells into a delicious, juicy fruit.
Single-seed fruits: Mangoes, peaches, and cherries guard one big sturdy seed inside.
Many-seed fruits: Watermelons, papayas, and apples carry dozens of tiny seeds.
Why fruits taste sweet: Animals eat the sweet fruit and help drop seeds in new places to grow.

pages.title: Seeds: Tiny Sleeping Wonders
bulletPoints: Seed coat: The tough outer jacket that protects the baby plant sleeping inside.
Cotyledon: The baby plant's packed lunchbox filled with starch and nutrients.
Embryo: The tiny living baby plant waiting for warmth and water to wake up.
Seed travelers: Dandelion seeds fly with fluffy parachutes; burrs hitchhike on puppy fur!

pages.title: Germination: A Baby Plant Wakes Up
bulletPoints: Step 1: The seed absorbs cool rain water and swells up big and round.
Step 2: The seed coat cracks open, and the tiny root (radicle) reaches down into the soil.
Step 3: The tiny green shoot (plumule) reaches up toward the warm yellow sun.
Step 4: Two tiny baby leaves unfurl, start making fresh food, and the seed coat falls off.

pages.title: What Every Plant Needs to Grow Happy
bulletPoints: Water: Gives life, keeps stems tall and crisp, and carries vitamins up from soil.
Sunlight: The warm energy source that powers green leaf kitchens.
Fresh Air: Clean carbon dioxide for making food and oxygen for nighttime breathing.
Rich Soil: Loamy brown earth full of earthworms, compost, and helpful minerals.

pages.title: Herbs, Shrubs & Trees: The Plant Family
bulletPoints: Herbs: Short plants with soft green delicate stems (mint, basil, spinach, cilantro).
Shrubs: Medium bushy plants with thin woody stems branching from the ground (rose, jasmine).
Trees: Tall, magnificent giants with thick wooden trunks and spreading canopies (banyan, mango, neem).
Climbers & Creepers: Peas that climb garden sticks and pumpkins that creep along the soil.

pages.title: Mighty Forest Canopies & Giant Trees
bulletPoints: The Banyan Tree: Sends down hanging aerial roots from branches that turn into new trunks!
Giant Redwood Trees: The tallest living trees on planet Earth, growing taller than skyscrapers.
Canopy layers: The forest roof where colorful macaws, monkeys, and tree frogs live.
Tree bark: Thick corky armor that shields giant trees from cold winter frost and forest bugs.

pages.title: Tree Rings: Counting a Tree's Age
bulletPoints: Inside every tree trunk are concentric circular rings telling its life story.
Light wide rings: Grown during sunny, rainy spring seasons when the tree grew quickly.
Dark narrow rings: Grown during dry winter months when growth slowed down.
Each pair of light and dark rings marks one full year of the tree's wondrous life!

pages.title: Water Plants: Floating Lilies & Lotus
bulletPoints: Lotus & Water Lilies: Float peacefully on ponds with wide waxy waterproof leaves.
Air pockets: Spongy hollow stems filled with trapped air keep water plants floating high.
Submerged waterweeds: Hydrilla grows completely underwater and makes bubble oxygen for fish.
Mangrove forests: Special trees with stilt roots that breathe air above salty coastal mud.

pages.title: Desert Plants: Thriving in the Hot Sand
bulletPoints: Cactus: Replaces flat leaves with sharp prickly spines to prevent precious water loss.
Fleshy green stems: Thick swollen stems store gallons of cool water through long dry droughts.
Widespread shallow roots: Dart out quickly in all directions to catch every drop of rare desert rain.
Waxy skin: A thick waterproof wax coating keeps desert succulents cool under scorching sun.

pages.title: Autumn Changes: Why Leaves Turn Golden
bulletPoints: As days grow shorter and cooler in autumn, trees prepare for a restful winter sleep.
Green chlorophyll slowly breaks down and disappears from the leaves.
Hidden colors shine through: Bright orange carotenes and golden yellow xanthophylls appear!
Deciduous trees shed their crisp dry leaves so heavy winter snow won't break branches.

pages.title: Evergreen Pine Trees: Surviving the Winter
bulletPoints: Needle-shaped leaves: Slender, waxy green needles that don't dry out in frosty winds.
Cone builders: Conifers like pine and cedar protect their seeds inside sturdy wooden pinecones.
A-frame shape: Sloping branches let heavy white winter snow slide right off to the ground.
Evergreen vitality: Keeping their needles green and healthy all twelve months of the year.

pages.title: Gifts from Our Plant Friends
bulletPoints: Tasty healthy food: Sweet apples, crunchy carrots, rice, wheat, and green broccoli.
Comfortable clothing: Soft fluffy cotton balls picked from cotton bushes make our shirts.
Sturdy wooden shelter: Furniture, pencils, books, paper, and musical violins from timber.
Fresh clean air: Absorbing smog and smoke while releasing fresh oxygen for all living creatures.

pages.title: Medicinal Plants & Healing Herbs
bulletPoints: Tulsi (Holy Basil): Soothing herbal leaves brewed in warm tea to cure colds and coughs.
Aloe Vera: Cool soothing jelly inside thick green leaves that heals sunburns and scratches.
Turmeric & Ginger: Golden underground roots with powerful anti-inflammatory healing power.
Neem Tree: Nature's natural antibacterial healer used for soothing skin and healthy teeth.

pages.title: Being a Guardian of Nature: Plant a Tree!
bulletPoints: Every big green forest began with small animals dropping tiny seeds in the dirt.
Planting a sapling: Dig a cozy hole, place the baby roots gently, water it, and give it love.
Watering schedule: Give plants a refreshing drink early in the morning before sun grows hot.
Promise to Earth: Protect green trees, water indoor plants, and celebrate the beauty of nature!
